title: Economy & Finance Stock–Flow–Obligation Network Atlas
purpose: Represent observable economic systems as linked balance sheets, flows, contracts, ownership/control, prices, production and dependencies rather than isolated headline numbers.

accounting_core.identity: Assets = Liabilities + Equity/net worth for a balance-sheet entity, subject to the accounting framework used.
accounting_core.flow_relation: Period income/receipts and expenses/payments change cash and net worth together with valuation and other adjustments.
accounting_core.sector_rule: One entity's financial asset is generally another entity's liability; sector consolidation removes internal positions.
accounting_core.time_rule: Every stock needs an as-of date; every flow needs a period.

edge_types.boundary: Control may arise without majority economic ownership.

risk_vectors.question: Can near-term payments be met without disorderly asset sales or emergency funding?
Do assets/income capacity plausibly cover liabilities/obligations over the relevant horizon?
How much debt must be rolled over and under what rate/market conditions?
Are obligations in a currency mismatched with revenues/assets?
How quickly do financing costs reset?
How dependent is the entity/system on a few customers, suppliers, lenders or markets?
What happens if a linked entity fails to perform?
How replaceable are critical inputs and routes?
How do revenues, expenditure, transfers, debt service and contingent liabilities interact?
How sensitive are balance sheets to market prices, exchange rates or accounting assumptions?

magnitude_contract.rule: Ratios require named numerator, denominator, period/date, units and source; unlike ratios must not be ranked as if interchangeable.

shock_propagation: price shock → income/cost change → cash flow → borrowing/investment/consumption response
rate shock → debt-service/refinancing change → balance-sheet response
supply disruption → inventory/production change → prices/substitution → trade/investment response
counterparty failure → credit loss/payment delay → liquidity/capital response → network spillover
policy/tax/transfer change → disposable resources/incentives → sectoral flows

worked_cases.title: Consolidation changes what a balance sheet means
worked_cases.observation: The Eurosystem annual consolidated balance sheet nets intra-Eurosystem positions while showing positions vis-à-vis third parties.
worked_cases.distinction: consolidated system balance sheet != simple sum of unconsolidated member balance sheets
worked_cases.lesson: Internal claims can disappear on consolidation even though they remain real for individual entities. Always ask what perimeter and eliminations produced the reported total.

worked_cases.title: A bank can hold assets and still fail from liquidity, rate risk and concentrated funding
worked_cases.observation: The Federal Reserve review identified governance and risk-management weaknesses, high uninsured-deposit concentration, interest-rate exposure and a rapid run as central elements of the failure.
distinctions: funding concentration matters alongside asset quality
worked_cases.lesson: A balance sheet cannot be read from total assets and liabilities alone; timing, market valuation, funding stability and behavioral response matter.
